QuestionStmt.S: The $E_{\text{cell}}^0$ of $\mathrm{Al(s) | Al^{3+}(1M) || Pb^{2+}(1M) | Pb(s)}$ cell is 1.5 V if $E_{\mathrm{Pb}^{2+}/\mathrm{Pb}}^0$ is $-0.14$ V then $E_{\mathrm{Al}^{3+}/\mathrm{Al}}^0$ will be

Solution.S:
For the cell

$$\mathrm{Al(s) | Al^{3+}(1M) || Pb^{2+}(1M) | Pb(s)}$$

the left side is the anode and the right side is the cathode.

So, aluminium undergoes oxidation and lead ion undergoes reduction.

For a cell,

$$E_{\text{cell}}^0 = E_{\text{cathode}}^0 - E_{\text{anode}}^0$$

Here,

$$E_{\text{cell}}^0 = 1.5 \text{ V}$$

$$E_{\text{cathode}}^0 = E_{\mathrm{Pb}^{2+}/\mathrm{Pb}}^0 = -0.14 \text{ V}$$

$$E_{\text{anode}}^0 = E_{\mathrm{Al}^{3+}/\mathrm{Al}}^0$$

Substitute the values:

$$1.5 = -0.14 - E_{\mathrm{Al}}^0$$

$$E_{\mathrm{Al}}^0 = -0.14 - 1.5$$

$$E_{\mathrm{Al}}^0 = -1.64 \text{ V}$$

Final Answer: $$\boxed{-1.64 \text{ V}}$$

Hence, the correct option is B.
